My best prediction is that it would change Ryan’s code from **SC to UA** and submit the list before noon. He says he wasn’t ill, and his sister—who lives elsewhere—isn’t within the stated DEP definition; the absence wasn’t booked in advance. The stated codes therefore leave UA as the literal fit, even though he called in and had an emergency.

That would give him a second UA during probation, so payroll would generate the termination letter. A free-text note might preserve his explanation but would not prevent that result. A cautious assistant should seek human review before allowing an automated dismissal, but the scenario offers no timely reviewer.
